newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FOCUS-New Zealand shares rally to record levels.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-New Zealand shares rally to record levels.

text.p: New Zealand share prices hit record highs on Monday following last week's budget and monetary policy statement, but some senior brokers doubted the rally's sustainability.

The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed at 2,501.96, up 58.7 points (2.4 percent) -- the highest level since its inception in 1991. Over the quarter just ended, the index has risen about 217 points or 9.52 percent.
Tim Preston, managing director at ANZ Securities (NZ) Ltd, said it appeared economic growth was set to rise.

"The market is a great barometer of future trends. I think what you're seeing...is a perception that perhaps the economy has bottomed and that you're going to start to see a gradual pickup in activity from here on," Preston said.
"If it's wrong, then some of these prices are not sustainable, but the money is on that we have seen the worst.
"Whether the market is right will start to unfold over the next three to six months."
There was increased liquidity washing around the market, possibly cash that had come out of fixed interest, plus the funds freed up from phase two of the Telecom buyback.
But there were questions about whether last week's budget and central bank easing were enough to get the economy out of the doldrums.
Brokers were well appraised of the likelihood that corporate earnings over the next couple of months were likely to be weak.
Mark Benseman, investment strategist at Merrill Lynch, said he thought the rally had pushed valuations to unsustainable levels and a retracement was likely.
He nevertheless regarded the rally as a healthy sign.

"If you take a two, three year view of the New Zealand market and the economy then I think it's still a good market to invest in, but I think tactically there is some opportunity however for the market to retrace.
"It's probably running a little ahead of itself at the moment and it's probably a good opportunity for a cooling off period," he said.
Campbell Stuart, head of equities at SBC Warburg, said that with GDP growth slowing there would be sectors that would not deliver.
"It becomes very stock selective. With GDP slowing down there are obviously some sectors out there that are not delivering," he said.

"There will be some earnings disappointments to come through, and so it will be important to be in the right stocks. In saying that, underlying valuations have increased with interest rates coming down," Stuart said.

Growth data released earlier in the session showed seasonally adjusted production-based GDP fell 0.5 percent in the March quarter, against a 0.7 percent rise in December and a rise of 1.0 percent in March 1996.
